summary: Satellites have recorded fire hotspots for 25 years, but the record is split across sensors that cannot be compared directly. Merge NASA FIRMS naively and burning in Türkiye appears to rise 67% when Suomi-NPP arrives, while Terra/MODIS, the one instrument that never changed, shows a 51% fall. TURQUA puts the whole record on one scale, what a single VIIRS satellite would count, and serves it as a web application: choose a country, province, drawn area or coordinate and a date range, and get a burning activity calendar, this month against its historical median, season, trend, anomalies and CSV downloads. Every reconstructed value carries a calibrated 80% interval. The method is checked with evidence: seams closed (×13.4 to ×1.13), ten held-out years reproduced at r = 0.989, satellite outages found and filled, and MODIS orbit drift measured from the hotspot timestamps. The same engine runs unchanged on Florida. Fire managers get a consistent picture of when and where burning happens, and a record that survives the retirement of MODIS.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

TURQUA is a web application that harmonizes NASA FIRMS MODIS and VIIRS hotspots into one burning activity calendar, 2001 to last month. Select Türkiye or Florida, one of 81 provinces, a polygon you draw, a latitude/longitude point or a box, and a date range. The page returns: a year-by-month calendar with accessible colour ramps; the latest month against the median of the same month in every earlier year; year-to-date and 12-month comparisons; the seasonal profile and the critical period that holds 80% of a typical year; a trend test; ranked anomalies; fire events with footprints on the NASA image of that day; and downloads (CSV calendar, CSV of hotspot cells found in the search, PNG, JSON analytics). Each value has an 80% interval and a confidence grade; months reconstructed from MODIS are hatched.

THE PROBLEM, MEASURED

Comparing 2009–2011 with 2012–2014, the merged archive for Türkiye rises 67% while Terra/MODIS alone falls 51%. Divided by Terra, whose orbit was held until 2021, raw hotspot counts spread ×13.4 as the constellation grows from one satellite to four. A calendar built on that is a calendar of satellites.

HOW IT WORKS

  1. Hotspots (vegetation fires only) become burning days: 36 km² H3 cells × local solar days. A burning day measures activity, not burned area.
  2. The target scale is one VIIRS satellite, Suomi-NPP. Its outages are detected by comparison with its twin NOAA-20, filled at the measured twin ratio, and flagged. The same rule continues the record after Suomi-NPP production ended on 2 November 2026.
  3. A transfer is learned where MODIS and VIIRS overlap (2013–2021), per land cover and calendar month, in two branches: where MODIS saw the cell, a multiplier; where it saw nothing, fire is placed by MODIS activity in the surrounding block.
  4. 2001–January 2012 is reconstructed from MODIS and given a calibrated interval; from February 2012 the calendar is measurement.
  5. A dependency-free Rust engine runs the pipeline with the full validation suite. The browser rebuilds the grid from the inputs and coefficients with the same formula and checks itself against the engine.

WHAT WE FOUND

  • Leave-one-year-out over ten years: national months reproduced at r = 0.989 (a plain MODIS-to-VIIRS ratio gives a clearly weaker fit); province-months also beat the plain ratio.
  • A measured ceiling: NOAA-20, the same sensor 50 minutes later, reproduces Suomi-NPP in a single cell-month at only r = 0.80; our method reaches 0.67 there. The rest is the physics of short fires, not the method.
  • Error bars that hold: on years the calibration never saw, 80% intervals contain the truth about 78–82% of the time at five scales.
  • The ruler is moving: read from the hotspot timestamps, Terra now crosses Türkiye at 09:19 local solar time instead of 10:57 and Aqua at 15:04 instead of 13:08 (measured at Turkish latitudes from FIRMS acquisition times, not the NASA nominal equator-crossing time). MODIS can no longer serve as a stable reference, and it is retiring.
  • From hotspots to fires: about 1.04 million hotspots become 443,744 fire events; the 2021 Manavgat megafire comes out as a single event.
  • Another continent: the same binary on Florida, with nothing tuned, closes the seams (×2.87 to ×1.07).

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO

It counts fires large and long enough to be seen. Burning days measure activity, not area. Reconstructed years carry about ±8% nationally and far more for one cell. The transfer is assumed stationary: true in Türkiye over the overlap, only roughly in Florida, where we report about ±10% bias in blocked tests. Cause-of-fire labels are not part of the calendar and are not validated.

WHO IT IS FOR

Fire and land managers, early-warning and emergency services, and scientists who need to know which months and years really burned more, whether this month is unusual, and when the critical period starts, without the satellite artefact and with an honest statement of confidence.

TOOLS

Rust (engine, no dependencies), Python (numpy, pandas, h3, rasterio) for ingest and packaging, plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript with MapLibre GL JS and h3-js for the application, NASA GIBS imagery, Netlify hosting.

PRIOR WORK

Before the event (October to 8 November 2026) we studied FIRMS data and built exploratory prototypes, including a public repository and a public demo site (published 8 November 2026). The method design, the validation approach and some key results (for example the hold-out correlation of 0.989) were first obtained in a pre-event Python prototype. During the hackathon (14–15 November 2026) we rebuilt the data pipeline, the Rust engine and the web application in a new repository and extended them with: a dependency-free Rust engine; detection of Suomi-NPP outages and filling from NOAA-20; the twin-satellite noise ceiling; the year-by-year orbit-drift measurement from hotspot timestamps; a live fire map from FIRMS near-real-time data; and two checks against ground records (Türkiye's official forest-fire counts and 7,589 reported Florida fires). Live application: https://turqua.netlify.app
